physics_disclosure: Stylized time-slowed 3D demonstration of tire-road contact; not a calibrated tire, vehicle dynamics or crash test

shots.narration_en: Those grooves can warn you before your car leaves the road.
shots.visual_proof: Detailed entire sedan enters milled shoulder groove strip
shots.mechanism_change: Vehicle travels forward toward recessed shoulder grooves

shots.narration_en: They are carved into the shoulder, not painted onto it.
shots.visual_proof: Actual depressed milling pockets with near-side front tyre visibly above
shots.mechanism_change: Tire approaches multiple genuinely recessed asphalt cuts

shots.narration_en: As a tire crosses the cuts, its contact with the road changes.
shots.visual_proof: Wheel rotates and road geometry passes below the tire
shots.mechanism_change: Wheel rotates based on absolute travelled distance; road contact oscillates

shots.narration_en: That makes a loud rumble and a vibration you can feel.
shots.visual_proof: Road pockets and moving tyre with small kinematic vertical response
shots.mechanism_change: Wheel passage drives a small vertical body vibration without fake sound-wave physics

shots.narration_en: The warning is meant to catch a drifting or drowsy driver's attention.
shots.visual_proof: Car, edge stripe and grooved shoulder are present together
shots.mechanism_change: Car continues across the shoulder groove zone

shots.narration_en: But it won't steer for you. The driver still has to react.
shots.visual_proof: Whole vehicle continues; grooves do not forcibly control steering
shots.mechanism_change: No automatic steering implied; continuous native motion ends safely
